articles.title: Clash Royale tabletop game surpasses $100,000 on Kickstarter after reaching target in one hour
articles.summary: Supercell and Maestro Media’s Clash Royale: The Grand Arena reached its Kickstarter funding goal in just one hour after launching the campaign on October 20th, 2026. The tabletop game raised $82,000 within that hour, more than three times the original $25,000 requested.... [ MORE ]
body: Fans can continue to support the game to reach stretch goals, potentially enabling upgraded acrylic standees and other surprises. At the time of writing, the game has already raised over $100,000.

The game supports two to four players, allowing them to command their forces, deploy cards, launch attacks and counter opponents as they fight to destroy Towers and collect Crowns. The player with the most Crowns wins.

The Grand Arena is expected to bring familiar Clash Royale characters and mechanics, with battles taking place across two lanes. Players must manage their Elixir stocks and can upgrade or add characters to their decks between battles.

Designed by David Gordon, Ryan Rodriguez and TAM, the tabletop game allows each player to choose a Champion around which to build an eight-card deck. Their Champion's evolution card will stay with them throughout the game, giving players a base for their strategy as battles progress.

articles.title: Supercell completes full acquisition of Metacore
articles.summary: Supercell has completed its acquisition of Metacore, taking 100% ownership of the Merge Mansion maker. The deal has brought Metacore’s games team into the fold, having "officially started their journey as Supercellians" supported by Supercell peers.
body: Supercell and Metacore originally announced the planned acquisition this May, when Supercell’s intentions to acquire the remainder of the Finnish studio and its flagship game went public. Supercell was already Metacore’s largest shareholder.
Alongside the purchase, Metacore announced it would be cutting up to 160 roles in Finland as part of a restructuring effort.

Months later, Supercell revealed the deal had been signed and that plans for Metacore’s integration were underway. It was expected that the deal would close at the end of September, but it has ultimately taken until today, October 19th, for an official announcement.

"We can finally share that the Supercell acquisition of Metacore and Merge Mansion has been closed. Merge Mansion will transition to be part of Supercell’s game portfolio, and Metacore is now 100% owned by Supercell," Metacore posted on LinkedIn.

articles.title: Supercell hit by cyberattack, but says no player data was affected
articles.summary: The Clash of Clans developer says it was the target of multiple attacks last week and has notified police and regulators.
body: Supercell has confirmed that an unauthorised party has accessed a platform Supercell used to host company meetings and presentations.

In an announcement on October 21, the Clash of Clans developer said it was targeted by multiple cyberattacks last week, one of which caused the incident. Based on its investigations so far, Supercell believes no player data was affected.

It says it blocked further access, took the service offline and began investigating the platform and its security experts. It has since filed a police report, submitted a notification under the EU Cyber Resilience Act, and notified the Data Protection Ombudsman, but said that because the investigation is ongoing, it cannot share further details at this time.

The videos include current and former employees, as well as some guests and partners who took part in internal events. They may contain people’s names, images and voices, and the names and email addresses of the platform’s users were also accessed.

articles.title: Supercell brings Clash Royale to tabletop with new Kickstarter board game
articles.summary: Supercell is bringing Clash Royale to the tabletop with Clash Royale: The Grand Arena, a board game developed with Maestro Media, set to launch on Kickstarter on October 20, 2026.
body: Designed by David Gordon, Ryan Rodriguez, and TAM, the game supports two to four players who can deploy cards, attack opponents and send their towers across two lanes.
Players will compete to destroy towers and collect crowns, the player holding the most crowns in the end wins.

The tabletop adaptation aims to retain several mechanics from the mobile game, including card-based strategy. Players build eight-card decks around a chosen champion, whose evolution card remains with them throughout the game. Players can upgrade or add characters to their decks between battles.

“Clash Royale has earned its place as a leading mobile strategy game by challenging players to think tactically, adapt, and outsmart their opponents,” said Andrea Fasulo, head of licensing at Supercell. “With The Grand Arena, our ambition is to honour that competitive spirit and strategic depth, giving fans a fresh challenge worthy of the game they love.”
